comparisons.peer_topic: Impairment measurement for assets held for use
comparisons.peer_summary: When indicators exist, the Company estimates future undiscounted cash flows; if insufficient to recover recorded value, assets are written down to fair value based on discounted cash flows or appraisals, with asset-generating ability being a key factor.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO discloses the valuation methodology for acquired developed technology (SoC controllers) using the relief-from-royalty method, whereas AMD discloses the accounting policy for impairment of assets held for use. While both relate to the valuation of intangible/tangible asset values, AVGO focuses on initial measurement via royalty forecasts, while AMD focuses on subsequent measurement via undiscounted cash flow tests for recoverability.

sentences.text: We valued the developed technology using the relief-from-royalty method under the income approach.
When indicators of impairment exist and assets are held for use, the Company estimates future undiscounted cash flows attributable to the related asset groups.

comparisons.peer_topic: Useful life estimation and January 2023 estimate change
comparisons.peer_summary: The company evaluates useful lives annually considering technology cadence and asset reuse, and effective January 2023, prospectively increased the estimated useful lives of certain wafer fabrication machinery from 5 to 8 years.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO determines the economic useful life of acquired developed technology based on the technology cycle, while INTC evaluates the useful lives of property, plant, and equipment annually considering process technology cadence. Both companies link asset useful life estimates to technology cycles/cadence, but AVGO applies this to acquired intangibles via the income approach, whereas INTC applies it to manufacturing assets affecting depreciation rates.

sentences.text: The economic useful life was determined based on the technology cycle related to each developed technology, as well as the cash flows over the forecast period.

At least annually, we evaluate the period over which we expect to recover the economic value of our property, plant, and equipment, considering factors such as the process technology cadence between node transitions, changes in machinery and equipment technology, and re-use of machinery and tools across each generation of process technology.

comparisons.peer_topic: Capitalization and Amortization of Product and Process Technology Costs
comparisons.peer_summary: The company capitalizes costs for acquiring product/process technology and patenting, amortizing them straight-line over up to 12.5 years, with amortization duration set to the shorter of the technology's useful life, patent term, or agreement term; fully-amortized assets are then removed from the books.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclose accounting policies for technology-related intangible assets. AVGO values developed technology using the relief-from-royalty method and assigns useful life based on technology cycles. MU capitalizes product/process technology costs and amortizes them straight-line over periods up to 12.5 years, with duration set to the shorter of the estimated useful life or patent term. Both identify 'technology' as the core asset class and link amortization/valuation lives to technology lifecycle constraints.

sentences.text: This method is based on the application of a royalty rate to forecasted revenue under the developed technology.
Product and process technology costs are amortized over the shorter of (1) the estimated useful life of the technology, (2) the patent term, or (3) the term of the technology agreement.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intangible Assets Composition and Amortization Policy
comparisons.peer_summary: Intangible assets primarily represent acquired developed technology, customer relationships, and licensed IP, which are amortized over periods ranging from one to twenty years using methods that reflect economic benefit consumption or straight-line if the pattern cannot be determined.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO discloses that developed technology (intangible assets) is valued using the income approach and amortized/used based on technology cycles. NVDA discloses that its intangible assets primarily include developed technology and are amortized over 1-20 years using methods reflecting economic benefit consumption. Both companies explicitly identify 'developed technology' as a primary component of their intangible assets and discuss the allocation of value/life based on economic benefit patterns or technology cycles.
